title: Priority-based constrained decoder + tokenizer escape handling for structured outputs
author: Samantha Ortiz
release_notes: Add priority ordering for constrained decoding backends and safe tokenizer-escape normalization. Streaming will now fallback to a lightweight sampling backend when constraints deadlock. Backwards-compatible by default.
description:
Motivation: Multiple customers hit flaky structured-output generation when combining grammar (CFG) and regex constraints plus tokenizer-level escapes. In practice this caused two problems: 1) when a grammar backend and a regex backend could both accept the same prefix, the selection was nondeterministic across shards leading to divergent streaming chunks, and 2) certain tokenizer edge-cases (escaped bytes, weird unicode combining marks) produced tokens that prevented the constraint checkers from matching, which broke JSON/structured parsing and function-calling payloads. This PR implements a stable, explicit priority ordering for constrained decoding backends, introduces a tokenizer escape normalization pass that runs prior to constraint evaluation, and adds a safe fallback sampling mode to keep streams alive when constraint logic would otherwise deadlock.

What changed (high level):
- Introduce a ConstraintPriorityManager that allows the runtime to evaluate backends in deterministic priority order (grammar -> regex -> lexical heuristics by default). The ordering is configurable per-request via the new "constraint_priority" field in the generation API; default behavior is backwards-compatible.
- Add a pre-evaluation TokenizerEscapeNormalizer that canonicalizes sequences likely to break matcher logic (escaped quotes, zero-width joiners, unicode decomposition). This processing is conservative and only affects how constraints are checked, not final emitted tokens.
- Implement a streaming failover: if constrained decoding for a token stalls for more than a configurable threshold (default 200ms extra), the runtime switches to a lightweight sampling backend that respects high-level constraints where possible and emits a special structured event ("constraint-fallback") downstream so clients can detect the behavior.
- OpenAI-compat: adjust function-calling codepath to prefer deterministic constraint backends when function schemas are present so returned arguments are less likely to be partially-formed across stream chunks.
- Extensive tests: unit tests for priority manager, token normalizer, integration tests that reproduce previously observed deadlocks, and e2e tests for OpenAI-compatible function calling with constrained outputs.

API changes and default behavior: The public API accepts an optional new field "constraint_priority" (array of strings) to allow customers to control backend ordering. If omitted, the system uses the safe default ordering included in this PR. No breaking changes to existing request payloads.
commits:
1) Add ConstraintPriorityManager + docs (S. Ortiz)
2) TokenizerEscapeNormalizer implementation + tests
3) Streaming fallback mode + metrics and event emission
4) OpenAI-compat adjustment to function-calling path
5) Add unit + integration + e2e tests and CI plumbing
6) Fix: edge-case for combining marks in tokenizer normalizer (follow-up)
reviews: Kenji Watanabe: Left a detailed review — requested clarifications on priority ordering and whether order should be per-model or per-request. Asked for more metrics around fallback frequency.

Samantha Ortiz: Reply — implemented per-request "constraint_priority" override, preserved model-level default mapping in ConstraintPriorityManager. Added metrics: constraint_evaluations, constraint_fallbacks, fallback_duration_ms.
Priya Narang: Questioned normalization side-effects on token probabilities. Requested a long-running canary for sampling fallback to validate quality degradation is acceptable.

Samantha Ortiz: Reply — TokenizerEscapeNormalizer only affects constraint matching input, not sampling distribution; added explicit tests asserting generation logits are unchanged. Added canary job in perf-canary to run for 48 hours post-merge.
Diego Morales: Approves after small nits (doc wording and one log line).
CI Bot: All tests passed on final push; one flaky test (test_streaming_timeout) was quarantined and ticketed (ENG-4215).
testing_notes: Added deterministic reproducer for the deadlock seen in SUP-887. Integration test simulates interleaved grammar+regex constraints across streaming shards and asserts no deadlock and that a single consistent token stream is produced. Canary will run post-merge to validate sampling fallback quality under traffic.
deploy_notes: Staged rollout: the ConstraintPriorityManager is feature-flagged off by default in Dedicated tenants until canary completes. Hosted API will enable default behavior immediately but expose the per-request override. Telemetry: emit constraint_priority_used and constraint_fallback events to the console stream.
compatibility_notes: Backwards compatible by default. OpenAI compatibility layer now prefers deterministic constraint backends when 'functions' are present; users relying on previous nondeterminism should pin explicit 'constraint_priority' if they want older behavior. No change to existing SDK method signatures; SDKs updated to surface the new parameter as optional.
